note: THREE LATE ARRIVALS COST HALF A DAY — the blueprint's own RL-ATT-001, published at last. `attendance.late_minutes` has been computed for every settled day since Phase 4 and, like overtime, nothing had ever read it: a person could be forty minutes late every morning of the month and the payslip would not know. SmartPRS 2 does have this rule, in `PayrollGenController::attendanceCut():449-455`, as a loop with the numbers written into it — which is why 'we give fifteen minutes, not ten' is a release there and a line in this file here.
policy_note: ALL_MATCH, from the decision point. A day can be penalised for lateness and for something else at once, and the penalties add — which is why APPLY_DAY_PENALTY is declared ADDITIVE in the action catalogue and why a policy that returned only the winner would quietly forgive one of them.

policy.late_grace_note: Minutes past the shift start before an arrival counts as LATE FOR THE PURPOSES OF THIS PENALTY. Deliberately not the same number as calendar.grace_minutes, which decides whether the day is marked late at all — an employer can mark somebody late at five minutes and only start penalising at ten, and collapsing the two numbers into one takes that choice away.

rules.name: Three late arrivals in a payroll month cost half a day
rules.description: The third and every later late arrival over the grace, within one payroll month, costs half a day of pay. Counted over the PAYROLL PERIOD rather than a rolling window, because that is the month the payslip is for and a rolling count would penalise a day twice across a month boundary.
rules.when:
attendance.late_minutes > policy.value('late_grace_min')
AND agg.count(late_arrival, payroll_period, { event.value > policy.value('late_grace_min') }) >= 3

then.reason: Third or later late arrival over the grace this payroll month
